observation: caseOnly is set on 2 of 156 confirmed findings
why_it_matters: The pre-registered design (proposal §5.1b, REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md) says a finding with no statable machine-checkable invariant is filed with caseOnly: true and does NOT gate convergence. That was the mechanism intended to stop the maintainability/preference tail from blocking forever, since preference judgments are an open space with no oracle. Critics almost never set the flag, so the IMPLEMENTED gate is strictly stricter than the DESIGNED gate: every suggestion gates.
reading: Blocking findings are trending down on lib (3,2,4,1,5,2,3,0,2,1 — three of the last four rounds at 0-2). Suggestions are not. If the caseOnly rule were applied as designed, the gate would already be close to firing on lib; as implemented, it is gated by the one category the design predicted would never saturate.
decision: The gating rule is NOT being changed mid-run. Relaxing a convergence criterion partway through, after seeing which category is blocking it, is precisely the failure E1 diagnosed — it would make any convergence claim unfalsifiable. The gap is recorded as a measured explanation for a loop that does not converge, and as the first thing to fix in a successor experiment rather than in this one.
